tasks.short: Direct bioinformatics technicians and IT staff

steps.what: Retrieve the current work packages, pipeline versions and open issues from {PROJECT}.
inputs: Existing staff-maintained work packages and issue records

steps.what: Read actual pipeline failures, sample restrictions and technical results against the research objectives.
inputs: Actual run reports and study objectives

steps.what: Discuss blockers, explain scientific requirements and coach technicians and IT staff on the actual work.
outputs: Shared understanding of the work and constraints

steps.what: Choose priorities, responsibilities and escalation paths in light of the staff discussion and scientific risks.
Record the actual assignments, owners and scientific acceptance criteria in {PROJECT}.
Save the work-package update in the same {PROJECT} record.

tasks.design: Configure a native {PROJECT} view that groups the existing work packages by study and pipeline version. The scientist still interprets failures, directs staff and writes the resulting assignments; saving that record has no approval stage or labour saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the relevant work packages can interrupt technical supervision.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing project filters and linked records can assemble the current scope without a model.
tasks.still_hard: A green run does not establish scientific validity or staff readiness.
tasks.human_edge: Diagnose scientific and interpersonal blockers and choose responsible priorities.

ambition.what: Protect technical supervision time; no new authority is assumed.

tasks.altitude: A small retrieval reduction; direction and accountability stay with the scientist.

reach.learn: Connect laboratory sample handling to computational acceptance criteria.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-3 for project permissions and any national consultation requirements

evidence.claim: Native project views can filter existing assignments and linked issues; they do not supervise scientific staff.

assumptions: Boundary is the scientist's direction cycle, including its actual assignment record. Staff execution and their existing record maintenance remain unchanged and receive no saving.

Existing staff records supply study id, work-package id, assignee, pipeline version, status and issue link. The scientist checks completeness in s1; missing records are requested and read manually, not extracted by an uncounted model.
Shares are conditional E1 estimates of these activities, not measured organisational baselines or fitted means priors. Only record navigation in s1 changes; native configuration is tested first.
The same-system save is represented at the schema's 1% resolution with full retained time and no self-approval. No extra report or notification baseline is assumed.
unknowns: Are current work packages complete enough for a useful native view?
research_questions: Does the view reduce navigation without hiding unresolved scientific issues?

already_counted.description: All remaining retrieval, technical assessment, supervision and assignment recording

incremental.description: Maintain study/version filters and check permissions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 4 minus 0.5 upkeep gives 3.5. Low 0 if the existing project view already groups the work and no new configuration is adopted; the supervision and writing remain in either scenario.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach selection and use of bioinformatics tools

steps.what: Locate the approved tool documentation, version-specific examples and training dataset in {DOCS}.
inputs: Existing approved tool documents and permitted training dataset

steps.what: Adapt the worked exercise and explanation to the learner's analysis question in {DOCS}.
Demonstrate tool selection and use, observe the learner's practice and explain limitations and unexpected outputs.
Write the actual exercise corrections and follow-up pointers in the teaching notes {DOCS}.
Save the teaching note in the same {DOCS} workspace.

tasks.design: Use native {DOCS} metadata and a version-indexed teaching collection to find approved worked examples. Keep tool selection, live instruction and actual follow-up writing human; no conversational agent certifies competence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Examples for different tool releases are easy to confuse.
tasks.enabler_now: Native version tags and filtered collections can narrow the source search.
tasks.still_hard: The learner must understand experimental assumptions and recognise misleading results.
tasks.human_edge: Explain why an apparently plausible analysis is inappropriate for this biological question.

ambition.what: Offer supervised introductory exercises to wet-lab researchers using permitted training data.

tasks.altitude: Less example hunting; teaching rights do not change.

reach.learn: Design exercises that connect sampling decisions with analysis assumptions.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-2 for training data and document access

evidence.claim: Document metadata can organise approved teaching material by software version; learner-specific explanation remains human work.

assumptions: Boundary is an actual instruction session and its worked exercise and follow-up note, not a newly invented recurring course administration process.

The scientist selects existing approved sources in s1 by tool, version, dataset identifier and exercise objective. Missing metadata is read manually; its repair is included in upkeep. Data owners already permit the training dataset; no genetic or patient data is sent to a new service.
Conditional E1 activity shares, not measured baselines. s1 retains source relevance checks; no software runtime or routine save earns a saving. Native search is tried before custom retrieval.
research_questions: Can a trainee distinguish a failed assumption from a tool error after the exercise?

already_counted.description: Retained source checking, adaptation, live teaching and actual follow-up writing

incremental.description: Repair example tags when tool versions change

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 6 minus 1 upkeep gives 5. Low 0 when the approved examples are already indexed or absent, so the scientist keeps the present search instead of adding the collection.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Observe researchers using the current bioinformatics interface and clarify problems with identifiers, units, cohorts and navigation.
inputs: Actual user tasks and observed problems

steps.what: Write the intended interface behaviour, permitted fields and known-input expected-output examples in {PROJECT}; test native interface settings first.
inputs: Existing permitted test dataset and current interface settings
outputs: Explicit change specification and scientist-authored test cases

steps.what: Implement the specified interface change on a development branch in the software-development workspace {OTHER}.
inputs: Change specification and test cases from s2

loop.purpose: Draft the bounded interface code change
loop.input: Permitted source, explicit specification and test cases from s2
loop.output: Local code diff with test results
loop.check: Scientist runs tests in s4; users test in s5; maintainer reviews the final diff in s7
loop.stop: One draft and one correction, then manual implementation; no merge or deployment tools
loop.why_not_simpler: Native settings are tested in s2; this branch covers a genuinely custom interaction, whose code depends on scientific identifier and cohort semantics.

steps.what: Run and inspect the actual tests, checking units, identifiers, cohort filters, access restrictions, accessibility and expected scientific outputs.
Observe researchers trying the draft interface on permitted test data and clarify usability failures.
Correct the code and rerun affected tests in the development workspace {OTHER}, producing the complete release candidate.
inputs: Actual defects from s4 and findings from s5
outputs: Final code diff and test evidence version v1

steps.what: Independently review the complete diff, test evidence and scientific-interface behaviour in {OTHER}, authorising that exact candidate for merge or returning defects.
inputs: Final code diff and test evidence v1 from s6
outputs: Independent merge decision bound to final candidate v1

steps.what: Save the final branch state in the same development workspace {OTHER}.
Merge only the independently authorised candidate into the maintained interface codebase {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Test native bioinformatics interface settings before adding code in {OTHER}. For a custom interaction, a bounded code-drafting loop works only on a development branch; scientific tests, user trials and an independent maintainer review precede the consequential merge.
tasks.previous_blocker: Custom interface changes require code as well as scientific understanding.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded code assistant can draft an explicit change against existing source and human-authored tests.
tasks.still_hard: A convenient filter can silently change the meaning of a cohort or expose restricted information.
tasks.human_edge: Define correct scientific behaviour and recognise misleading interactions.

ambition.what: Provide a tested cohort-selection interface for researchers who cannot write database queries.

tasks.altitude: More time for scientific usability; no new release or clinical decision authority.

reach.learn: Translate clinical research cohort definitions into testable interface constraints.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-10 for source access, data safeguards and release governance

evidence.claim: A bounded code assistant can draft interface changes, but scientific semantics and access control require human tests and review.

assumptions: Boundary includes interface development, actual testing and the usual independently reviewed merge. Production deployment, where separate, keeps its existing maintainer procedure and earns no saving.

The custom-code scenario assumes an existing maintainer review, not an author self-approval stage. Other-role review is retained at 8 shares and excluded from the scientist's 92-share baseline; no free review transfer is claimed.

s2 produces the exact field definitions, allowed cohort operations and expected outputs on an existing permitted test dataset. If those cannot be specified, implementation remains manual. No free test-data synthesis or unrestricted genetic-data feed is assumed.

Conditional E1 step estimates; source/test access must be permitted before any model use. A failed or changed candidate returns to s6 and receives fresh s7 review before s9. The internal branch save has no gate and no saving.
unknowns: Can native settings solve the issue?
Are there existing test fixtures and independent code review?
research_questions: Does the change preserve cohort membership, access boundaries and researcher understanding on held-out examples?

already_counted.description: Retained scientist specification, implementation review, tests, user trials, corrections and commits
Existing independent review, shown outside the scientist denominator

incremental.description: Refresh regression cases and audit assistant-produced dependencies

approvals.approved_version: Exact final candidate v1 and test evidence from s6, unchanged at s8; any edit voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Scientist baseline 92, gross 10/92*100 = 10.87; minus 2 upkeep gives 8.87. High rounded down to 8.8. Low 0 when custom code is too small or semantic defects remove the drafting benefit and the assistant is not adopted. Native-only changes need a separate measured baseline.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Clarify the actual operational problem with researchers and IT staff: reproducibility, queue delays, sample lineage or access constraints.
Find existing architecture, pipeline and process documentation in {DOCS} relevant to the actual problem.
inputs: Existing current process and architecture documents

steps.what: Evaluate new bioinformatics systems and processes to improve operations against actual scientific validity, migration effort, data safeguards and operational constraints.
inputs: Actual problem and criteria from s1

steps.what: Recommend new systems and processes to improve bioinformatics operations in {DOCS}, writing the alternatives, dependencies and evidence limits.
Discuss the complete recommendation with the research decision maker, answering questions about evidence and uncertainty.
Save the actual recommendation in the same {DOCS} workspace.

tasks.design: Configure native {DOCS} views and version filters to find the current process evidence. Keep evaluation, written recommendations and discussion human; the result is advice, not automatic procurement or production changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Current process evidence is scattered across study and platform documentation.
tasks.enabler_now: Metadata and version filtering can reduce navigation while preserving original evidence.
tasks.still_hard: A tool change may improve throughput while weakening reproducibility or sample lineage.
tasks.human_edge: Weigh scientific risks and organisational adoption against operational convenience.

ambition.what: Revisit the specific recurring pipeline bottleneck using the same documented decision criteria.

tasks.altitude: Evidence is easier to locate; recommendation and investment rights do not change.

reach.learn: Map wet-lab handoffs to computational lineage and failure modes.

evidence.claim: Native document version filters can reduce source navigation; they cannot establish scientific or financial value of an operational change.

assumptions: Boundary is actual investigation, recommendation writing and discussion. No procurement, invented ROI study or extra sign-off process is added.

Existing document owners supply system name, process area, study id, version and source link. s2 checks relevance and currentness; absent metadata means manual reading with no claimed gain for that source.

Shares are conditional E1 activity estimates. Only source navigation is changed; no saving is attributed to same-system storage or existing software runtime. Native configuration precedes any custom index.
unknowns: Are process documents current and versioned?
Who can authorise the recommended operational change?
research_questions: Does easier source access change investigation effort without encouraging unsupported cost or scientific claims?

already_counted.description: Remaining evidence checks, evaluation, actual recommendation writing and discussion

incremental.description: Maintain process tags and remove obsolete source links

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 6 minus 1 upkeep gives 5. Low 0 if current documents are already linked or cannot be indexed reliably, so the present investigation method remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: A scientist who spends less time finding versioned records and drafting bounded interface code, while keeping scientific direction and recommendations.
reach: Connect biological technician procedures with computational acceptance criteria
Help medical scientists express testable cohort-selection requirements
role.ambitious_version: A research team with usable, tested analysis interfaces and clearer laboratory-to-computation handoffs.
